subject: food-technology
title: Macronutrients in Depth: Foundations
welcome_lead: Meet the three macronutrients — carbohydrates, proteins and fats — and what each one does.
meta_desc: GCSE macronutrient foundations: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, recommended intakes.
final_note: Macronutrients give energy and build the body — both matter.

concepts.def: Nutrient needed in large amounts for energy.
Main energy source from sugars and starches.
Single or double sugar unit, fast energy.
Long chain of sugars, slower energy release.

walkthroughs.body_html: Carbohydrates are the body's preferred fuel. Simple sugars in fruit and sweets give a fast spike of energy. Complex starches in bread, pasta and potatoes are broken down more slowly, giving steadier energy across the day.

Protein is essential for growth, repair and enzymes. It is made of amino acids; adults need 8 essential ones from food and children need 9. Animal foods are usually complete sources; plants often need combining.

Fats are the most energy-dense macronutrient at about 9 kcal/g, compared with 4 kcal/g for protein and carbohydrate. They insulate organs, carry vitamins A, D, E and K, and provide essential fatty acids the body cannot make.
